name: Classic Buttercream Rosettes
description: Dense, hand-piped buttercream rosettes covering part or all of the cake in a swirled, textural pattern.
techniqueNotes: Piped with a large closed star tip in tight overlapping rows; needs a firm, well-chilled buttercream that holds a sharp swirl in warm rooms.

name: Fresh Floral Cascade
description: An asymmetrical waterfall of fresh flowers and greenery flowing down one side of the tiers.
techniqueNotes: Flowers are inserted in food-safe floral picks or piping-gel-sealed stems directly into the frosting, never bare stems into cake.

name: Fondant Lace
description: Delicate edible lace panels or appliqués applied over a smooth fondant base, mimicking bridal lace fabric.
techniqueNotes: Cast in a silicone lace mat from a lace-mix (fondant + tylose/CMC), dried flat, then adhered to the tier with edible glue.

name: Sugar Flower Sculptural
description: Hand-sculpted gum-paste flowers built petal by petal to be nearly indistinguishable from fresh blooms, arranged as a structural feature.
techniqueNotes: Petals are rolled paper-thin, wired, and dusted with edible powder color, then assembled and dried before being wired onto the cake — a days-long process done well ahead of the event.

name: Modern Geometric
description: Sharp-edged fondant panels, angular color-blocking, or repeating line and chevron patterns that read as architecture rather than decoration.
techniqueNotes: Panels are cut from templates for exact symmetry and applied to a perfectly smooth fondant or ganache base — any surface imperfection is highly visible at this level of precision.

name: Watercolor Painted
description: Soft, blended washes of edible color hand-painted directly onto fondant, mimicking a watercolor wash on paper.
techniqueNotes: Petal dust or gel color is diluted with clear alcohol (which evaporates cleanly, unlike water) and layered in thin translucent washes with a soft brush.

name: Metallic Drip
description: A controlled ganache or candy-melt drip down the sides of each tier, finished with a metallic gold or bronze luster.
techniqueNotes: The drip's temperature and consistency have to be tested on a spare piece before committing — too warm and it runs off the base entirely, too cool and it clings without falling.

name: Naked Rustic Berries
description: A bare or semi-naked exterior with the sponge layers left visible, dressed simply with fresh berries and a few sprigs of herb or greenery.
techniqueNotes: A single thin 'crumb coat' scrape of buttercream is applied and left as the final finish rather than smoothed further, so the sponge shows through deliberately.
